main_body: Snow-roofed stone well: a stone well body with a dark water opening and brown posts, under a snow-covered roof
top_band: Pale grey rim around a dark opening ellipse, rows ~16-22. The snow roof above it (rows 1-9) is also a light top surface.
evidence: The opening reads as a dark elliptical pool with a brown bucket or plank, seen from above and framed by a lighter stone rim (rows 16-22). Below it a darker row at the rim's edge leads into the stone front face (rows 23-31). The snow roof is a wide lighter slab with a visible front edge and icicles. The front-face bands are painted flat rather than inset, but the opening is clearly seen from above, so the 3/4 structure holds.

style.evidence: The snow has several steps (white, pale blue, blue-grey), the stone has 4 greys with dither, and the wood posts have 3 browns. Outlines lean blue-grey or brown with the material rather than being uniform black. The lower stone bands are a bit stripy and flat compared with the reference well, but there is no large flat fill and the piece would sit acceptably beside the reference.
